## Experimental design

The 100 experiments are organized as **50 matched pairs**. In each pair the edit is the same. The two parent cells differ mainly in whether one condition holds, so any difference in the edit's effect points to an interaction rather than the edit's average effect. There are 10 themes, with 5 pairs each:

| # | Edit | Condition contrasted | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–10 | edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 | edges 2 and 4 both `none` (node 1 is a dead end) vs. not | A conv feeding an unused node should be wasted |
| 11–20 | edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 5 = `none` (node 2 is not connected to the output) vs. not | Same dead-end logic for node 2 |
| 21–30 | edge 5 → none | edge 3 = `none` vs. skip/conv | Removing 2→3 hurts more when there is no direct 0→3 path |
| 31–40 | edge 3 → skip_connect | edge 5 = nor_conv_3x3 (deep conv path) vs. weak edge 5 | A residual shortcut may help most alongside a deep conv path |
| 41–50 | edge j → avg_pool_3x3 | the op being replaced is a conv (k=j) vs. skip | Losing a conv should cost more than losing a skip |
| 51–60 | edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 0 = `none` (node 1 carries zeros) vs. not | The 1→3 conv only matters if node 1 receives input |
| 61–70 | edge 3 → none | edge 5 = `none` vs. not | Removing 0→3 is risky when 2→3 is also absent |
| 71–80 | edge 2 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 0 = `none` vs. not | The 1→2 conv depends on node 1 having input |
| 81–90 | edge 5 → skip_connect | it replaces nor_conv_3x3 vs. replaces `none` | The same edit could be harmful or beneficial depending on what it replaces |
| 91–100 | edge 0 → skip_connect | edge 3 = skip_connect vs. conv/pool/none | Redundant shortcuts vs. the only shortcut |

I'll propose the 10 hypotheses next.
